page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-96 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine instance designed for workloads requiring dedicated hardware acceleration. This server type is engineered to support demanding graphical and parallel computing tasks by combining high-density CPU resources with professional-grade graphics processing units.

The hardware configuration features 96 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 360.0 GB of system memory, which yields a ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via two integrated NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs. This instance does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached block storage options. Additionally, it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4-standard-96 offers a specialized resource profile that balances a high vCPU count with dual professional GPUs. This configuration is optimized for resource-intensive visual computing rather than general-purpose storage-heavy tasks. The lack of local storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring users to factor in the performance and cost of external storage volumes for data-heavy operations.

This instance is suited for workloads such as high-end 3D rendering, computer-aided design, video encoding, virtual workstation hosting, and moderately sized machine learning inference tasks that benefit from professional GPU acceleration and substantial system memory.
